name: Block Editor Navigator for WordPress – Post Navigation, Quick Edit & Search Plugin
author: Krasen Slavov

sections.description:
Navigate between WordPress posts instantly with Block Editor Navigator – the productivity plugin that adds Previous/Next post navigation and instant search directly in the WordPress editor.

Stop wasting time clicking back to post lists. Block Editor Navigator adds Previous/Next navigation buttons directly in the WordPress Block Editor, letting you move between posts, pages, and custom post types without leaving the editor screen. Built-in instant search helps you find any content in seconds, streamlining your WordPress editing workflow.

Whether you’re managing blog posts, editing WooCommerce products, or working with custom post types, Block Editor Navigator saves hours by eliminating unnecessary clicks and page loads.

Why Choose Block Editor Navigator?

  • WordPress Post Navigation – Previous/Next buttons in Block Editor
  • Instant Search – Find posts instantly with autocomplete search
  • Quick Edit Posts – Navigate and edit posts without leaving editor
  • Gutenberg Navigation – Native WordPress Block Editor integration
  • Classic Editor Support – Works with both Gutenberg and Classic Editor
  • WooCommerce Compatible – Navigate WooCommerce products easily

How WordPress Post Navigation Works

  1. Install and activate Block Editor Navigator on your WordPress site
  2. Edit any post or page in the WordPress Block Editor
  3. Look for Navigator Controls panel in the right sidebar
  4. Click Previous or Next to navigate between posts
  5. Use Search button to find posts instantly
  6. Jump to any post without returning to admin dashboard

Zero configuration required – works immediately with WordPress posts, pages, and custom post types.

Perfect For

  • Content Managers editing multiple WordPress posts daily
  • Blog Authors navigating large content libraries
  • WooCommerce Store Owners managing product catalogs efficiently
  • WordPress Developers working with custom post types
  • Productivity Enthusiasts streamlining WordPress workflows
  • WordPress Agencies managing client content efficiently

WordPress Post Navigation Features

Post Navigation in Block Editor
Navigate WordPress posts chronologically with Previous and Next buttons directly in the Gutenberg editor. Move forward or backward through posts without returning to the WordPress admin dashboard. Perfect for editing multiple posts sequentially or reviewing content in order.

Instant WordPress Post Search
Built-in autocomplete search finds WordPress posts, pages, and custom post types instantly. Type any keyword and see matching results appear immediately. Click any result to navigate directly to that post in the WordPress editor – no page reload required.

WordPress Quick Edit
Edit WordPress posts faster by eliminating unnecessary navigation. Jump between posts, pages, and custom post types without leaving the editor screen. Save hours of clicking back and forth between admin lists and edit screens.

Gutenberg Post Navigator
Native WordPress Block Editor integration adds Navigator Controls panel directly in the Gutenberg sidebar. No separate windows or popups – everything works seamlessly within the WordPress Block Editor interface you already know.

Classic Editor Post Navigation
Full WordPress Classic Editor support with Navigator Controls metabox. Previous/Next buttons and instant search work identically in Classic Editor, providing consistent post navigation regardless of which WordPress editor you prefer.

Custom Post Type Navigation
Navigate any registered WordPress custom post type including WooCommerce products, portfolios, testimonials, and more. Enable/disable post navigation for specific post types in plugin settings for complete control over your WordPress workflow.

Usage

Once the WordPress post navigation plugin is installed and activated:

  1. Edit any post or page in WordPress Block Editor (Gutenberg)
  2. Look for Navigator Controls panel in the right sidebar
  3. Click Previous or Next to navigate between posts
  4. Click Search button to open instant search
  5. Type keywords to find posts and click results to navigate
  6. Continue editing without returning to WordPress admin

Here are the steps to use Block Editor Navigator:

  1. Open Editor – Edit any WordPress post or page in Block Editor
  2. Find Controls – Locate Navigator Controls panel in sidebar
  3. Navigate Posts – Click Previous/Next to move between posts
  4. Search Posts – Use instant search to find any post by keyword
  5. Quick Edit – Jump to any post and continue editing immediately

Note: Recent Posts tracking and Favorites features currently support Posts and Pages only. Custom post type support coming in version 1.4.0.

WordPress Post Navigation Settings

Block Editor (Gutenberg) Settings:
1. Edit any WordPress post in Block Editor
2. Find Navigator Controls panel in right sidebar
3. Click Previous to go to previous post chronologically
4. Click Next to go to next post chronologically
5. Click Search to open instant post search
6. Type keywords and click results to navigate

Classic Editor Settings:
1. Edit any WordPress post in Classic Editor
2. Find Navigator Controls metabox on the page
3. Use Previous, Next, and Search buttons identically to Block Editor
4. Navigate posts without leaving Classic Editor screen

Global Plugin Settings:
1. Go to Settings > Block Editor Navigator
2. Editor Controls – Enable/disable for Block Editor or Classic Editor
3. Post Type Controls – Choose which post types show navigation (Posts, Pages, Products, Custom Post Types)
4. Save settings to apply WordPress post navigation preferences

Supported WordPress Post Types:
– Posts
– Pages
– WooCommerce Products
– Custom Post Types
– All registered post types

Features & Limitations

The Block Editor Navigator WordPress post navigation plugin allows you to:

  • Navigate WordPress posts with Previous/Next buttons in Block Editor
  • Search posts instantly with autocomplete in WordPress editor
  • Quick edit WordPress posts without leaving editor screen
  • Navigate WooCommerce products efficiently in Gutenberg
  • Move between custom post types without returning to admin
  • Enable post navigation for specific WordPress post types
  • Use post navigation in both Block Editor and Classic Editor
  • Search posts, pages, and custom post types by keyword
  • Navigate posts chronologically forward and backward
  • Boost WordPress editing productivity and workflow efficiency
  • Access post navigation in WordPress multisite networks

WordPress Post Navigation Components

Previous/Next Buttons
Navigate WordPress posts chronologically with intuitive Previous and Next buttons. Move backward to older posts or forward to newer posts without leaving the WordPress editor. Buttons appear directly in Block Editor sidebar for instant access.

Instant Post Search
Autocomplete search finds WordPress posts as you type. Enter keywords and see matching posts, pages, and custom post types appear instantly. Click any result to navigate directly to that post in the WordPress editor with no page reload.

Navigator Controls Panel
Native WordPress Gutenberg integration adds Navigator Controls panel to Block Editor sidebar. All post navigation features accessible in one convenient location without cluttering your WordPress editing interface.

Classic Editor Integration
WordPress Classic Editor gets Navigator Controls metabox with identical functionality. Previous/Next buttons and instant search work seamlessly in Classic Editor for consistent post navigation experience.

Post Type Flexibility
Enable WordPress post navigation for any registered post type. Configure plugin settings to show navigation controls on Posts, Pages, WooCommerce Products, or custom post types individually.

Productivity Optimization
Eliminates clicking back to WordPress admin post lists. Navigate and quick edit posts directly in Block Editor, saving time and reducing unnecessary page loads during WordPress content management.

Known Limitations

Current version features:

  • Post Navigation – Previous/Next buttons work with all WordPress post types
  • Instant Search – Search works with Posts, Pages, Products, and Custom Post Types
  • Recent Posts – Currently limited to Posts and Pages (Custom post types in v1.4.0)
  • Favorites – Currently limited to Posts and Pages (Custom post types in v1.4.0)
  • Editor Support – Full Block Editor and Classic Editor compatibility
  • Post Types – Works with all registered WordPress post types
  • Multisite – Fully compatible with WordPress multisite networks
  • Performance – Optimized loading only on WordPress editor screens

Detailed Documentation

Find step-by-step setup guides, video tutorials, WordPress productivity tips, and navigation best practices on the Block Editor Navigator Documentation page.
sections.installation:
Installing the WordPress post navigation plugin is straightforward. Contact support if you encounter any issues.

Requirements:
– WordPress 5.0 or higher
– PHP 7.2 or higher
– Gutenberg Block Editor or Classic Editor

Installation from WordPress

  1. Go to Plugins > Add New
  2. Search for Block Editor Navigator
  3. Click Install Now then Activate
  4. Navigate to Settings > Block Editor Navigator (optional)
  5. Edit any post to see Navigator Controls

Manual Installation

  1. Download the WordPress post navigation plugin ZIP file
  2. Upload the block-editor-navigator folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  3. Go to Plugins in WordPress admin
  4. Activate Block Editor Navigator
  5. Navigate to Settings > Block Editor Navigator (optional)

After Activation

The plugin works immediately! You’ll see Navigator Controls when editing any WordPress post or page. To customize settings:

  1. Go to Settings > Block Editor Navigator
  2. Choose editor support (Block Editor / Classic Editor)
  3. Select post types for navigation (Posts, Pages, Products, Custom Post Types)
  4. Save settings to apply WordPress post navigation preferences
  5. Edit any post to use Previous/Next navigation and instant search

Quick Start:
1. Edit any WordPress post
2. Find Navigator Controls in sidebar
3. Click Previous or Next
4. Navigate posts instantly!
sections.faq:
Visit the Support Forum to share your questions or requests.

We usually respond to tickets within a few business days.

Feature requests are added to our wish list and considered for future updates.

How do I navigate between posts in WordPress?

Install Block Editor Navigator, edit any post in WordPress Block Editor, find the Navigator Controls panel in the sidebar, and click Previous or Next buttons to move between posts without leaving the editor.

What’s the best WordPress post navigation plugin?

Block Editor Navigator provides simple, lightweight post navigation for WordPress. Previous/Next buttons in Gutenberg, instant search, and quick edit functionality make it ideal for WordPress content managers who edit multiple posts regularly.

How to quick edit posts in WordPress?

Install Block Editor Navigator and use Previous/Next navigation to move between WordPress posts directly in the editor. No need to return to admin post lists – edit posts sequentially with one-click navigation.

Does this work with Gutenberg Block Editor?

Yes, Block Editor Navigator is designed specifically for WordPress Gutenberg. The Navigator Controls panel integrates natively into the Block Editor sidebar with Previous/Next buttons and instant post search.

Can I use this with Classic Editor?

Yes, full WordPress Classic Editor support is included. Navigator Controls metabox appears when editing posts in Classic Editor with identical Previous/Next navigation and search functionality.

How to search posts in WordPress editor?

Open any post in WordPress Block Editor, find Navigator Controls panel, click the Search button, type keywords, and see matching posts appear instantly. Click any result to navigate to that post immediately.

Does this work with WooCommerce products?

Yes, enable WooCommerce Products in Settings > Block Editor Navigator under Post Type Controls. Navigate WooCommerce product posts with Previous/Next buttons and instant search in the WordPress editor.

Can I navigate custom post types?

Yes, Block Editor Navigator works with all registered WordPress custom post types. Enable specific post types in plugin settings to add post navigation to portfolios, testimonials, projects, or any custom content.

Will this slow down my WordPress site?

No, the plugin is optimized for WordPress performance. Scripts only load on editor screens (not frontend), ensuring minimal impact on site speed. Lightweight code with efficient WordPress queries.

How to navigate posts chronologically in WordPress?

Click Previous to move backward to older posts or Next to move forward to newer posts. Block Editor Navigator navigates WordPress posts in chronological order based on publication date.

Can I disable navigation for specific post types?

Yes, go to Settings > Block Editor Navigator, find Post Type Controls, and uncheck any post types where you don’t want navigation buttons to appear in the WordPress editor.

Does this work with WordPress Multisite?

Yes, Block Editor Navigator is fully tested and compatible with WordPress multisite networks. Post navigation works identically across all sites in your WordPress multisite installation.

How to find posts quickly in WordPress?

Use the instant search feature in Navigator Controls. Type any keyword and matching WordPress posts appear immediately in autocomplete results. Click any post to navigate directly to the editor.

Can I navigate between pages in WordPress?

Yes, Block Editor Navigator works with WordPress posts, pages, and all custom post types. Enable Pages in post type settings to add Previous/Next navigation and search to WordPress page editing.

Does this replace WordPress admin post lists?

No, Block Editor Navigator complements WordPress admin by adding post navigation directly in the editor. You can still access admin post lists anytime, but for sequential editing, navigation buttons eliminate unnecessary clicks.

Is there a keyboard shortcut for post navigation?

Keyboard shortcuts are planned for a future version. Currently, use Previous/Next buttons in the Navigator Controls panel to navigate WordPress posts.
